source.title: When do Convolutional Neural Networks Stop Learning?
source.authors: Sahan Ahmad; Gabriel Trahan; Aminul Islam

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Figure contents are not rendered in the text; Figure 5 is represented by its caption and the authors' description.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures test accuracy across training epochs for three CNNs, using an epoch sweep rather than directly testing the fall-rise-fall test-error curve described in V2.
record.gate_note: The double-descent statements in the introduction and related work are background claims, not results from this study. Figure 5 is the study's own epoch-wise test-accuracy result; its numerical curve values are unavailable in the text. The stopping-epoch accuracy comparisons in Tables 4 and 5 do not establish the shape of an epoch-wise curve and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The paper proposes a stopping rule for CNN training based on layer activation variation. It mentions double descent only in passing, in the introduction and related work, citing Belkin et al. [6]. Figure 5 sweeps epochs (10–200) for three CNNs on CIFAR10, and Figure 4 plots validation error over 200 epochs for ResNet18. Neither result is analysed for a fall-rise-fall shape: the authors say only that accuracy reaches a stable stage and that the gap does not significantly increase. No curve values are given, and there is no label noise or model-size sweep. These results serve the authors' own stopping method and do not test V2 or any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that a layerwise activation-stability rule, using no validation data, anticipates a near-optimal stopping epoch. They report it saves 58.49% of computation on average across six CNN variants on CIFAR10, CIFAR100 and SVHN. On ten medical datasets they report about 44.1% saving against MedMNIST-V2 without losing accuracy. They make no claim about double descent.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a layerwise activation-variation stability rule to stop CNN training and an epoch-wise accuracy analysis; it does not conduct the model-size/interpolation sweep described by the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: The stability rule depends on rounding precision r: r=1 causes very early stopping; r=3 does not guarantee stopping at near-optimal capacity; r>3 may not stop training even after many epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR10, test accuracy for ResNet18, VGG16 and CNN is described as plateauing after some epochs (Figure 5). The ResNet18 validation error is described as not rising significantly over 200 epochs (Figure 4). No values are given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under standard training without label noise, test accuracy of CIFAR10 CNNs plateaus over epochs rather than showing a second descent.

record.problems: The text supplies no numerical Figure 5 curve values, and the described stable-stage result is insufficient to determine whether accuracy first falls, rises, then falls over epochs. The epoch-wise analysis covers only three CNNs on CIFAR10.
record.rows_left_out: Tables 4 and 5 report accuracy and computation comparisons for the proposed stopping rule against fixed-epoch training, but these do not report the epoch-wise curve shape tested by V2. Other stability-vector plots and numerical values describe the stopping measure rather than test error over epochs.

untested.parts: No test of an epoch-wise fall-rise-fall shape. The epoch sweeps (Figures 4 and 5) are described only as a plateau, with no values and no label noise.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No effective-complexity measure is tested. The stability vector is a stopping heuristic.
No label noise, regularization tuning or multiple-peak analysis.

record.verdict_notes: Double descent appears only as cited background: CNNs 'behave like a double-descent curve', citing [6]. Figure 4 (validation error over epochs) is described in words only. It is not a double-descent test, and its setup has no label noise. The Table 4 and 5 accuracy comparisons evaluate the authors' own method against fixed-epoch training and are rightly left out as rows.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or test-error measurement across model sizes.

Tests test accuracy over epochs for ResNet18, VGG16, and CNN on CIFAR10 only. The extracted text does not provide curve values or describe whether there is a fall-rise-fall shape, nor whether any peak is near interpolation.
No training-sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweep across model classes testing general double descent.
The study uses a layerwise stability measure to choose a stopping epoch but does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak locations across size, epochs, and samples.
No test of label noise, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
No comparison against an effective parameter count or test of whether that measure turns second descent into a U-shaped curve.
